dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. Good morning, how can I help you?
Hello, yes, good morning. Thank you for picking up. My name is Samir Rahman. I am calling about the storm drain by my house. It is flooding again, and it is the same problem every time it rains.
Okay, Mr. Rahman, I'm sorry to hear that. Let me get some details. What's the address?
It is 251 Callender Avenue. In the North End. Two, five, one.
Two fifty-one Callender Avenue, North End. Got it. And you said it keeps happening. Was this after the storm over the weekend?

Yes, yes, the nor'easter. Last weekend, Saturday into Sunday. It is Wednesday now, so three days, and it is still bad. Nobody has come to look at it. Every storm, same thing, and I am the one who has to deal with it.
Understood. So tell me what you're seeing out there. Is the drain itself blocked, or is it the water pooling?

Both, I think. The drain at the curb is clogged, full of leaves and, um, sand. And at the bottom of the driveway, the apron, there is a puddle that just sits. It does not go to the street. It drains toward the garage door. So the water goes the wrong way, to the garage.
So the apron at the end of your driveway holds water, and it slopes back toward the garage door. Let me make sure I have that right, the water's heading toward the garage, not away.
Correct, correct. Toward the garage. Thank you for repeating.
Sure. Is any water getting inside the garage right now?

A little at the door, wet at the bottom. Not inside much yet. But if it rains again, I do not know. And the sidewalk, it is a sheet of mud and grit. All the dirt came out of the street and the drain and now it is all over the sidewalk. People are slipping. I almost slipped myself.
A sheet of mud and grit on the sidewalk in front of the house. Okay. I'm writing that down along with the clogged catch basin at the curb.
Yes. Catch basin, yes, that is the word. The one at the curb. Sorry, one moment.
No problem, take your time.
[pause] Okay. The phone is, um, it is a cordless one and it beeps when the battery is low. If it beeps, that is not you. That is my phone.
Ha, okay, thanks for the warning. Then let me grab your callback number now in case it cuts out. What's the best number?
Yes, good idea. It is 401-555-0168.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-six-eight. Is that right?
Yes, that is right. Thank you.
And are you the owner there, or do you rent?
I rent. The landlord does not do anything about the street. It is the city's drain, so I am calling you.

That's fine, you can absolutely report it. The catch basin in the street is ours. The driveway apron, depending on how it's graded, may be partly on your property side, but I'll have the crew look at the whole spot and note it.
Okay. But it keeps happening. Every storm. I have called before, I think, or my neighbor did. I do not know. Nothing changes.

I hear you. I don't have a record in front of me of what was done before, but I'm putting this in as a drain backup with the sidewalk debris, and I'll mark that it's a repeat complaint from the neighborhood.
Thank you, thank you. That is good. When will they come?
The crews are working through a long list after the storm. I'd say within the next several days to a week is realistic. If it's sooner, great.
A week. Okay. [pause] That is long, but okay. Please, I would like a call back when it is done. So I know they really went.

Yes, I'll put a note on the work order asking for a callback to the number you gave me when it's completed. Let me read back what I have. Two fifty-one Callender Avenue. Clogged storm drain at the curb, water pooling on the driveway apron draining toward the garage door, and mud and grit covering the sidewalk. Callback to Samir Rahman at the number ending oh-one-six-eight.
Yes, all correct. Very good. Thank you for checking each thing.
Of course. And if the water starts coming into the garage in a real way, or it's raining hard and the street is flooding, call us right back so we can flag it.
I will. Oh, the battery, it is beeping. I think I should go. Thank you, Miss Lorraine, thank you very much.
You're welcome, Mr. Rahman. Take care.
